summary: Lane County, OR platform on Siuslaw NF; dates conflict (c.1919 platform vs 1930s pole tower); listed abandoned, last described as standing in 1994; no source says gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as abandoned; the most recent source describing the structure dates from 1994, when it was still there.

events.note: Open platform on round pole legs, dated c.1919 by the Oregon lookouts history; firelookout.com dates a pole tower to the 1930s instead
Roads under construction to Fairview Mountain and Cummins Peak, per a Nov. 1, 1934 Register-Guard item quoted by the Oregon lookouts history
Described as still there; listed as abandoned

evidence.supports: Siuslaw National Forest is the agency
c.1919 open platform with round pole legs
evidence.quote: c.1919: An open platform with round pole legs.
Railroad spikes were used for steps on the northwest corner.

evidence.supports: 1930s 15-foot pole tower with 6x6 platform; abandoned; still there 1994
evidence.quote: 1930s: 15' pole tower w/ 6x6' platform. Abandoned. Still there 1994.
The lookout roads are being built to Fairview mountain and Cummins peak.

evidence.supports: the Register-Guard item is dated November 1, 1934

corrections.why: Both sources describe the lookout as abandoned; Fire Lookout says it was still there in 1994, and neither says it was removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon lookouts history dates an open platform to about 1919; Fire Lookout describes a 15-foot pole tower with a 6-by-6-foot platform from the 1930s. The two may describe different structures or different dates. The story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: The record's status 'gone' is not supported by any source read; sources say abandoned, last described as standing in 1994. Do not confuse with Fairview Peak, a different lookout (Umpqua NF; cherylhill.net lists it as standing). An Oregon Digital photo record titled 'Fire lookout platform on Fairview Peak. Structure collapsed about 1990' appeared in search but could not be fetched (SSL certificate error) and names a different peak, so it is not used. No staffing, access, or current-condition source found.
